core_obligations: Record that the monomorphism and factorisation assumptions give that the reductions of the source and the target agree (proof lines 6206-6208).
Reduce to an affine target: check that the four assumptions are preserved by etale base change, and use the etale-local characterisation of closed immersions (proof lines 6210-6214).

For an affine target written as a filtered colimit of affine schemes, show that the base changes of the morphism are affine schemes with monomorphisms inducing isomorphisms on reductions, and conclude that it suffices to treat a monomorphism of affine schemes inducing an isomorphism on reductions (proof lines 6216-6225).

Note that the general statement fails without the last assumption, by reference to a counterexample, and that under the last assumption the corresponding ring map is either of finite type or has a Noetherian source while becoming an isomorphism modulo the nil radical (proof lines 6227-6240).

Conclude surjectivity of the ring map in the two cases, by the criterion modulo a locally nilpotent ideal and by Nakayama's lemma respectively, and hence that the original morphism is a closed immersion (proof lines 6242-6247).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to an affine target (proof lines 6210-6214).
Reduction to a monomorphism of affine schemes (proof lines 6216-6225).
The case split and why the last assumption is needed (proof lines 6227-6240).
Surjectivity by the two criteria (proof lines 6242-6247).
difficulty_reason: For a morphism of formal algebraic spaces that is representable, a monomorphism, factors the inclusion of the reduction of the target, and is either locally of finite type or has a locally Noetherian target, the lemma concludes that it is a closed immersion (statement lines 6193-6204). The proof first records the consequence of the monomorphism and factorisation assumptions, namely that the reductions of the two sides coincide (proof lines 6206-6208). It then reduces to an affine target: the assumptions are preserved by etale base change, so the etale-local characterisation of closed immersions lets the target be assumed affine (proof lines 6210-6214). Writing that affine formal algebraic space as a filtered colimit of affine schemes, the base changes of the morphism are algebraic spaces carrying monomorphisms that induce isomorphisms on reductions, and a statement on limits of spaces makes them affine schemes; it therefore suffices to treat the case of a monomorphism of affine schemes inducing an isomorphism on reductions (proof lines 6216-6225). That case is where the last assumption enters: the author notes that without it the conclusion is false, referring to a published counterexample, and then observes that either the morphism is of finite type or the target is Noetherian, so that the corresponding ring map has the property that its reduction modulo the nil radical is an isomorphism and is either of finite type or has a Noetherian source; surjectivity then follows from the criterion for a surjection modulo a locally nilpotent ideal in the first case and from Nakayama's lemma, applied because the nil radical is finitely generated and therefore nilpotent, in the second (proof lines 6227-6247). The claim is H2: one reduction and one case split are carried out, the counterexample in the general case is acknowledged, and the two case analyses each invoke a distinct named criterion.
